subject: VPC upgrade playline and contingency sync
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Brooks <samantha.brooks@harborbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: VPC upgrade playline and contingency sync

Samantha —

Thanks again for carving time this morning. Attached is a concise playline we discussed for your private fleet upgrade: short canary slices, an out-of-band telemetry snapshot before any cutover, and a two-hour narrow maintenance window per cluster. The attachment (upgrade-runbook-v1.2.pdf) has the step-by-step and the gating criteria we want to run during each slice.

A couple of points I want to flag explicitly:
- Version pinning: we recommend pinning control-plane components to v1.19.4 for the first wave and holding inference runtime at the customer-stable build (rwinf-2026-11-27) for 48 hours post-canary before broader unpin.
- Network cordon / traffic fencing: netops will apply a temporary routing ACL to preserve ingress control while we validate external TLS termination. This reduces blast radius for KV cache misses.
- Rollback triggers: explicit thresholds in the runbook — error rate spike > 2.5x baseline OR tail latency P95 regression > 40% for more than 3 consecutive minutes.

Can you confirm the narrow windows below work on your side and whether the HarborBank infra team prefers a single weekend slice or weekday night windows?

Proposed narrow windows (each cluster):
- Cluster A: Fri 22:00–24:00 PST
- Cluster B: Sat 01:00–03:00 PST
- Cluster C: Sat 04:00–06:00 PST

If those look OK, I'll open a scheduled change in HB-CRM-1345 with the canary CSV and share the runbook link.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: upgrade-runbook-v1.2.pdf, network-drift-checklist.xlsx
From: Samantha Brooks <samantha.brooks@harborbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: HarborBank Infra <ops+infra@harborbank.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade playline and contingency sync

Thanks, Irene —

Appreciate the clear steps. A few quick responses from infra:
- Weekday narrow windows preferred (less overlap with batch jobs). Can we instead do Cluster A: Mon 23:00–01:00, Cluster B: Tue 00:30–02:30, Cluster C: Tue 03:00–05:00 PST?
- Netops will run the routing ACL in staging first and produce a short netflow capture (we'll share the link).
- Regarding version pinning: HarborBank security insists on a documented rollback timeline of no more than 60 minutes to full traffic revert for customer-facing ingress — is that achievable with the current runbook?

Two asks from our side before we sign off on the change:
1) Confirm your canary gating artifact (we'll need the exact metrics and the threshold definitions in a machine-readable format so our SRE automation can enforce them).
2) Provide a one-line description of the rollback command set and the lead on-call's mobile number so we can expedite emergency reversion.

If you can ingest the minor scheduling tweak above, we can schedule the upgrade for the week of Dec 21.

—Sam
Samantha Brooks
Head of Infrastructure Operations
HarborBank

Attachment referenced: HB-netflow-sample.pcap (will upload to your Drive link)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Brooks <samantha.brooks@harborbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade playline and contingency sync

Sam — thanks for the clarifications, good catches. Responses inline: 

- Scheduling: weekday windows work; we'll update the CSV and change ticket to:
  * Cluster A: Mon 23:00–01:00 PST
  * Cluster B: Tue 00:30–02:30 PST
  * Cluster C: Tue 03:00–05:00 PST

- 60-minute rollback SLA: short answer — yes, provided we keep the canary size conservative and have the netops ACL pre-staged. The runbook includes a pre-baked revert that does three things: (1) circuit-breaker activation to stop new traffic to updated nodes, (2) a single-command service reconfiguration to repoint the load-balancer back to the pinned control-plane, and (3) a KV cache warm-start from snapshot. Time estimates: 15–25 minutes for LB repoint, 10–20 minutes for KV warm-start depending on working set, additional buffer for health checks (~10 min). We'll document this as the '60-minute emergency revert'.

- Canary gating artifact: Karthik — can you attach the gating JSON that the platform will publish for automation? It should include metrics, windowing rules, and exact thresholds. Monica — please add the on-call roster and the primary mobile for the revert owner to the runbook.

Next steps: Karthik will upload gating JSON; Monica will update roster; I'll push the updated canary schedule CSV and the revised runbook link to HB-CRM-1345. Once we have netflow sample from HarborBank we'll run a quick staging ACL test.

If everyone is aligned I'll mark this 'ready-for-scheduling' by EOD.

Thanks —
Irene

Adding the gating JSON (summary below) for automation — full file will be uploaded to the runbook link within the hour.

Gating summary (human-readable):
- metrics: error_rate_total, p95_latency_ms, rollout_429_count
- canary_size: 5% traffic split for 30 minutes, then 20% for 30 minutes before full release
- thresholds: error_rate_total <= 2.5x baseline; p95_latency_ms <= 1.4x baseline; rollout_429_count increase <= +10/minute
- rollback_window: immediate abort if any threshold breach persists for 3 consecutive minutes; emergency revert command: 'rwinf rollback --target snapshot:hb-20261211-precanary'

Monica — roster? Also adding Aditya to the watchlist for post-release telemetry tuning.

I'll post the machine-readable JSON to: https://drive.redwood.com/ops/runbooks/upgrade-runbook-v1.2/gating.json and attach to HB-CRM-1345.

-Karthik
